answer: Nectar-Ledger Work Receipts. Each identity must publish a signed, publicly checkable history of completed work, and payments flow only along that receipt chain; a clone starts with an empty chain and earns nothing. Like a vine, valid history must graft onto an existing verified root, so forgery requires redoing all prior tasks. Fresh identities also face a tundra period of delayed payouts and higher dispute exposure. Cloning costs the full duplicated work history per identity, making honesty cheaper.
